title: Frontline onramp for enterprise feature asks: routing, quick-scope, and scoring
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success teams regularly surface high-touch feature requests from enterprise prospects and customers. Today those asks are scattered across Slack threads, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc emails. PMs lack consistent first-pass context (business value, compliance constraints, rough complexity) which slows triage, inflates discovery cycles, and introduces bias toward well-networked accounts.

Objective: Create a lightweight frontline 'onramp' that converts a sales/cs ask into a structured Linear ticket with an automatic prioritization score and a minimal scoping payload. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-response to <=48 hours, enable consistent prioritization decisions by PM, and capture signal for Dedicated/Private deployment needs.

Scope: MVP covers high-touch (enterprise-tier) non-bug feature requests that originate from Sales, CS, or Solutions Engineering. Excludes internal tooling and project work initiated by engineering.

Proposed components:
1) Intake form (single-page): account name, AE/CS owner, ask summary (one sentence), use case narrative (3-5 bullets), revenue signal (ACV or deal stage), expected go-live timeframe, data sensitivity tags (PII, regulated, FTC/FINRA etc), desired deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), customer-provided SLA targets, estimated business impact (low/medium/high), suggested priority (AE), attachments (mockups/requirements).

2) Auto-enrichment and scoring: hook into account metadata (tier, MRR/ACV estimate, open deals) + product telemetry (active API calls, endpoints used) to auto-populate fields. Scoring rubric (weights): revenue potential (30%), reach (25%), compliance/regulatory (20%), technical complexity estimate (15%), strategic alignment (10%). Score buckets: 0-39 (Low), 40-69 (Medium), 70-100 (High).

3) Quick-scope payload: short templated fields that become the ticket body: business objective, representative acceptance criteria (3 max), surface-level tech risks, likely dependencies (infra, runtime change, private deployment), suggested fallback (workaround), initial rough sizing label (Spike / S / M / L with ballpark dev weeks).

4) Routing rules and SLA: requests scoring High -> PM High-Touch queue (PM review within 48 hours); Medium -> backlog triage slot (next weekly intake); Low -> auto-ack + CS playbook for workaround. Provide an option for AE to mark request as 'sales-critical' to override routing (requires justification).

5) Automation: integrated button in Salesforce and a Slack slash-command (/enterprise-ask) that pre-fills the form. Submissions create a Linear ticket with standardized tags and post a summary to #pm-intake with an action card.

6) Pilot and metrics: 6-week pilot with 5 AE/CS reps and 3 solutions engineers. Metrics: time-to-first-response, conversion rate from ask -> scoped project, proportion of asks with complete scoping fields, # of duplicates consolidated, and downstream time-to-release for accepted features.

Why this is different: Instead of only clustering asks after they land, this design moves signal capture upstream at the first touch, enforces minimal scoping discipline, and provides an objective first-pass ranking to reduce bias and churn.

Risks & trade-offs: the scoring will sometimes misclassify strategic-but-low-revenue asks; to mitigate, we include manual override with required justification. Over-burdening sales with long forms will reduce adoption — design must prioritize speed (<=4 min to complete). Auto-enrichment requires reliable product/account telemetry which is currently partial; fallback is a short manual input path.

Open questions: permitted data fields in Salesforce -> legal privacy review? Do we capture exact ACV or ranges? Should the scoring surface customer segmentation separately for Dedicated/Private needs?
acceptance_criteria: Frontline intake form implemented in Salesforce and available via Slack slash command
Submissions automatically create Linear tickets with PM-42786 tag and populated quick-scope fields
Auto-scoring runs on submission and assigns a High/Medium/Low bucket visible on the ticket
Routing automation posts a summary to #pm-intake and assigns to correct PM queue within 48 hours for High-scoring asks
Pilot dashboard available in Console showing time-to-first-response, completeness rate, and scoring distribution

comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Drafted intake fields and initial scoring rubric. Shared with Sales leaders for quick sanity check. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/Frontline+Onramp+Draft

2026-02-25 Priya Nair (Design): Recommend reducing open-text fields; replace free-form use case with 3 structured checkboxes + optional example customer journey to speed completion. Also suggested inline help for 'data sensitivity' tags.

2026-03-03 Luca Moretti (Eng): Auto-enrichment needs a stable source of truth for ACV. Proposed fallback: accept ACV-range with three buckets (<100k, 100k-1M, >1M). Raised ENG-1842 as dependency for telemetry API.

2026-03-07 Samir Patel (PM Director): Reviewed scoring weights; suggested increasing regulatory weight to 25% for Q2 given sales pipeline in finance customers. Approved pilot with 5 reps. Added goal: achieve 60% complete scoping fields in pilot.
2026-03-10 Oliver Grant: Implemented Slack prototype and basic Linear creation webhook. Demo recorded: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/slack-prototype-demo

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Updated flow to include 'sales-critical' override and requirement to add justification. Legal flagged storing exact ACV in Salesforce; switching to ACV range to avoid privacy review delay.
